arxiv-2311-14097.title: ACT-Diffusion: Efficient Adversarial Consistency Training for One-step Diffusion Models
arxiv-2311-14097.creator: Fei Kong Jinhao Duan Lichao Sun Hao Cheng Renjing Xu, Hengtao Shen Xiaofeng Zhu Xiaoshuang Shi Kaidi Xu
arxiv-2311-14097.description: Abstract Though diffusion models excel in image generation, their step-by-step denoising leads to slow generation speeds. Consistency training addresses this issue with single-step sampling but often produces lower-quality generations and requires high training costs. In this paper, we show that optimizing consistency training loss minimizes the Wasserstein distance between target and generated distributions.

arxiv-2406-00576.title: A Universal Transfer Theorem for Convex Optimization Algorithms Using Inexact First-order Oracles
arxiv-2406-00576.creator: Phillip Kerger, Marco Molinaro, Hongyi Jiang, Amitabh Basu
arxiv-2406-00576.description: Abstract Given any algorithm for convex optimization that uses exact first-order information (i.e., function values and subgradients), we show how to use such an algorithm to solve the problem with access to inexact first-order information. This is done in a “black-box” manner without knowledge of the internal workings of the algorithm.

Views and opinions expressed are however those of the author(s) only and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or the European Research Council Executive
arxiv-2407-07051.creator: Radu Curticapean, Daniel Neuen
arxiv-2407-07051.description: Abstract For a fixed graph property Φ \Phi and integer k ≥ 1 k\geq 1 , consider the problem of counting the induced k k -vertex subgraphs satisfying Φ \Phi in an input graph G G . This problem can be solved by brute-force in time O ⁡ ( n k ) O(n^{k}) .

arxiv-2410-23862.title: ψ \psi DAG: Projected Stochastic Approximation Iteration for DAG Structure Learning
arxiv-2410-23862.creator: Klea Ziu, Slavomír Hanzely, Loka Li, Kun Zhang, Martin Takáč, Dmitry Kamzolov
arxiv-2410-23862.description: Abstract Learning the structure of Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) presents a significant challenge due to the vast combinatorial search space of possible graphs, which scales exponentially with the number of nodes. Recent advancements have redefined this problem as a continuous optimization task by incorporating differentiable acyclicity constraints.

arxiv-2502-03235.title: Bubbles clustered inside for almost critical problems
arxiv-2502-03235.creator: Mohamed Ben Ayed, Khalil El Mehdi a : Department of Mathematics, College of Science, Qassim University, Buraydah 51542, Saudi Arabiab : Faculté des Sciences et Techniques, Université de Nouakchott, Nouakchott 2373, Mauritania.
arxiv-2502-03235.description: Abstract Abstract: We investigate the existence of blowing-up solutions of the following almost critical problem -\Delta u+V(x)u=u^{p-\varepsilon},\quad u>0\quad\mbox{in}\quad\Omega,\quad u=0\quad\mbox{on}\quad\partial\Omega, where \Omega is a bounded regular domain in \mathbb{R}^{n} , n\geq 4 , \varepsilon is a small positive parameter, p+1=(2n)/(n-2) is the critical Soblolev exponent and the potential V is a smooth positive function.

We present a multitask surrogate for neutron-star equations of state (EoSs) that delivers distribution-free , certified uncertainty via split conformal prediction (CP) and its Mondrian variant.

pmc-10518082.title: Comparison of different surgical treatments for stage II progressive collapsing foot deformity: a finite element analysis
pmc-10518082.creator: Fanglin Chen, Chengjie Yuan, Mian Liang, Guoping Le, Jian Xu
pmc-10518082.description: BackgroundThis study analyzed the advantages and disadvantages of different procedures for stage IIA progressive collapsing foot deformity (PCFD) through three-dimensional finite element models.MethodsA previous validated stage IIA PCFD FEA model was established consisting of 16 bones, 56 ligaments, 5 muscles and soft tissues.

pmc-11549892.title: Protopine Exerts Neuroprotective Effects on Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Brain Damage in Rats via Activation of the AMPK/PGC1α Pathway
pmc-11549892.creator: Liying Lu, Mengdan Pang, Tingting Chen, Yingying Hu, Likai Chen, Xiaoyue Tao, Shangqin Chen, Jianghu Zhu, Mingchu Fang, XiaoLing Guo, Zhenlang Lin
pmc-11549892.description: IntroductionNeonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), caused by perinatal asphyxia, is characterized by high morbidity and mortality, but there are still no effective therapeutic drugs. Mitochondrial biogenesis and apoptosis play key roles in the pathogenesis of HIE. Protopine (Pro), an isoquinoline alkaloid, has anti-apoptotic and neuro-protective effects. However, the protective roles of Pro on neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury remain unclear.

pmc-11588396.title: Orthostatic hypotension in a patient with HIV: uncovering adrenal insufficiency from fluticasone–cobicistat interactions
pmc-11588396.creator: Serena Dienes, Robert Nunn, Alison Lai
pmc-11588396.description: cobicistat-containing antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimens, inhaled corticosteroids have the potential to cause adverse effects, and these medication combinations should be avoided. In patients taking cobicistat-containing antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimens, inhaled corticosteroids have the potential to cause adverse effects, and these medication combinations should be avoided.

pmc-11594869.title: Co-Occurrence of Psoriasis and Asthma in the Pediatric Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11594869.creator: Mateusz Mleczko, Agnieszka Gerkowicz, Dorota Krasowska
pmc-11594869.description: Introduction: The risk of asthma in patients with psoriasis and that of psoriasis in patients with asthma have increased, but relevant data for the pediatric population are lacking. Therefore, we performed a meta-analysis to assess the pooled association between psoriasis and asthma in children and adolescents.

pmc-11657348.title: DNEA: an R package for fast and versatile data-driven network analysis of metabolomics data
pmc-11657348.creator: Christopher Patsalis, Gayatri Iyer, Marci Brandenburg, Alla Karnovsky, George Michailidis
pmc-11657348.description: BackgroundMetabolomics is a high-throughput technology that measures small molecule metabolites in cells, tissues or biofluids. Analysis of metabolomics data is a multi-step process that involves data processing, quality control and normalization, followed by statistical and bioinformatics analysis. The latter step often involves pathway analysis to aid biological interpretation of the data.

pmc-12382081.title: Determinants of uncontrolled seizures among pediatric epilepsy patients in Debre Tabor comprehensive specialized hospitals Ethiopia
pmc-12382081.creator: Tigabu Eskeziya Zerihun, Fisseha Nigussie Dagnew, Sisay Sitotaw Anberbr, Getachew Yitayew Tarekegn, Abel Temeche Kassaw
pmc-12382081.description: BackgroundThe cornerstone of achieving remission for epileptic patients is anti-seizure medication (ASM). An effective anti-seizure pharmaceutical therapy can lead to seizure independence by reducing or eliminating symptoms. This study aimed to evaluate treatment outcomes for epilepsy and related factors among pediatric patients in Debre Tabor Comprehensive specialized Hospital.MethodA cross-sectional study involving 300 children with epilepsy was conducted.

pmc-12489276.title: Constraint‐based metabolic modeling reveals metabolic properties underpinning the unprecedented growth of Chlorella ohadii
pmc-12489276.creator: Fayaz Soleymani, Sandra Marcela Correa, Marius Arend, Niayesh Forghanisardaghi, Haim Treves, Zahra Razaghi‐Moghadam, Zoran Nikoloski
pmc-12489276.description: Summary Comparative molecular and physiological analyses of organisms from one taxonomic group grown under similar conditions offer a strategy to identify gene targets for trait improvement. While this strategy can also be performed in silico using genome‐scale metabolic models for the compared organisms, we continue to lack solutions for the de novo generation of such models, particularly for eukaryotes.

pmc-12588566.title: All-photon logic gate calculation based on phase change materials
pmc-12588566.creator: Jiapeng Sun, Jinhua Mou, Jiaxing Gao, Jianwei Wang, Yuxin Liu, Wei Jin, Yu Zhang, Lu Liu, Hanyang Li, Zhihai Liu
pmc-12588566.description: Information modulation plays a crucial role in the contemporary development of photonic information networks. However, prevailing optical modulators exhibit challenges such as structural complexity, high cost, elevated insertion losses, and crosstalk issues in optoelectronic conversion. To address these concerns, we propose a novel all-photonic non-volatile fiber device based on Ge2Sb2Te5 (GST), integrating a dual peanut-shaped microstructure and GST.

pmc-12589514.title: Relationship between body positivity and body neutrality with body image, self-esteem, mindfulness and gratitude
pmc-12589514.creator: Anna Lipińska
pmc-12589514.description: Despite the growing popularity of body positivity and body neutrality on social media, their scientific differentiation remains unclear. Body positivity involves acceptance and a positive attitude toward one’s body regardless of societal ideals, whereas body neutrality emphasizes a non-judgmental focus on body functionality.

pmc-12661283.title: Functional/dissociative seizures: Proposal for a new diagnostic label and definition by the ILAE task force
pmc-12661283.creator: Coraline Hingray, Stoyan Popkirov, Kasia Kozlowska, Chrisma Pretorius, Mercedes Sarudiansky, Wissam El‐Hage, Dong Zhou, Deniz Ertan, LaFrance WC, Markus Reuber, the ILAE Functional/Dissociative Seizures Task Force
pmc-12661283.description: The acceptability and validity of the term "psychogenic nonepileptic seizures" (PNES) have been questioned. Currently, numerous alternative terms, such as “conversion,” “dissociative,” “functional,” “attacks,” and “events,” are used in both medical literature and clinical practice, leading to confusion among professionals and patients. The lack of a uniform diagnostic label is likely to impede research funding and service development.

pmc-12741578.title: Associations Between Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms and Inflammatory Factors: Insights From a Two‐Sample Mendelian Randomization Analysis
pmc-12741578.creator: Huimin Guo, Yu Li, Bowei Liu, Songtao Liu, Yunhao Li
pmc-12741578.description: PurposeInflammation is implicated in the pathogenesis of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP‐NENs); however, the causal nature of this association remains unclear. This study sought to evaluate the causal relationships between GEP‐NENs and inflammatory factors using a two‐sample Mendelian randomization (MR) approach.

pmc-13084403.title: Ion channel and biophysical properties of extracellular vesicles
pmc-13084403.creator: Shridhar Kiran Sanghvi, Harpreet Singh
pmc-13084403.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are a heterogeneous population of lipid bilayer–enclosed particles secreted by nearly all cell types into the extracellular milieu. Once considered cellular debris, EVs are now recognized as biologically active entities capable of transferring proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids to recipient cells, thereby modulating their function and contributing to intercellular communication.

pmc-13198368.title: Effects of Bacillus licheniformis 809 and Bacillus subtilis 810 supplementation on in situ degradation of a high-concentrate byproduct-based diet in forage-fed beef cows
pmc-13198368.creator: Arnaldo C Limede, Rodrigo S Marques, Fernando A A Cidrini, Erollykens F Santos, Paolo Fantinati, Bruno I Cappellozza
pmc-13198368.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study evaluated the effects of Bacillus-based direct-fed microbial (DFM) supplementation on in situ nutrient disappearance and degradability of high-concentrate diets. Fifteen rumen-cannulated cows were used in a completely randomized design. Treatments consisted of a forage-based diet plus 500 g of protein-mineral (390 g dried distillers grain + 110 g vitamin-mineral mix; as-fed basis) supplement mixed with 1) 3 g (as-fed basis) of a Bacillus-based DFM containing Bacillus licheniformis 809 and B.

pmc-13211083.title: AD-DETR: A Real-Time Transformer with Multi-Scale Alignment and Spatial–Spectral Fusion for Crop Disease Detection
pmc-13211083.creator: Bingyang Wang, Huibo Zhou, Zhi Wang, Ruolan Chen
pmc-13211083.description: Agriculture faces significant challenges from crop diseases, which threaten global food security and cause substantial economic losses annually. While deep learning has advanced plant disease detection, existing models often struggle with generalization across heterogeneous environments and real-time deployment constraints, hindering their practical application in diverse agricultural settings.

pmc-13346985.title: Integrated mineralogical, microstructural, and thermal characterization of Azara barite Nasarawa State, Nigeria and its implications for radiation shielding materials
pmc-13346985.creator: Nuraddeen Nasiru Garba, Muhammad Dahiru Audu, Rabiu Nasiru, Umar Ahmadu, Usman Musa Kankara, Jamilu Usman, Bashir Yusuf, Abdullahi Muhammad Vatsa, Musa Jibril
pmc-13346985.description: This study presents a comprehensive physicochemical, structural, and thermal characterization of barite ore obtained from the Azara deposit in Nasarawa State, Nigeria, with the aim of evaluating its properties relevant to radiation shielding materials. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis revealed barite (BaSO₄) as the dominant crystalline phase, with minor contributions from associated minerals including graphite, silicon oxide, and anhydrite.

pmc-13380756.title: Vasculopathy as a mechanical barrier to cancer spread: Clinical evidence and a rheology-based model in lung cancer and other solid tumors
pmc-13380756.creator: Giulia M Stella, Cristina Novy, Francesco Rocco Bertuccio, Ilaria Ferrarotti, Valentina Conio, Chandra Bortolotto, Tiziana Giorgiani, Lucrezia Pisanu, Ilaria Salzillo, Annalisa De Silvestri, Vittorio Arici, Alice Maccarini, Pietro Cerveri, Angelo G Corsico, Antonio Bozzani
pmc-13380756.description: Highlights•In a retrospective cohort of patients affected by PAD and cancer, an unexpectedly low metastatic burden at diagnosis was documented.•Monte Carlo simulations support the existence of a threshold beyond which vascular and rheological alterations become metastasis-inhibiting.•The results of this work unveil a novel conceptual link between vascular pathology, blood rheology and cancer progression.

pmc-13534177.title: The Smoky Stick Insect: Defensive Chemicals From a Vietnamese Phasmatodean (Necrosciinae: Neohirasea catbaensis)
pmc-13534177.creator: Marco Niekampf, Till Beuerle, Paul Meyer, Sven Bradler, Thomas Schmitt
pmc-13534177.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Beyond their impressive repertoire of camouflage as the predominant primary defensive strategy, stick and leaf insects (Phasmatodea) can actively defend themselves chemically with deterrent substances emitted from a pair of prothoracic repellent glands. The Vietnamese Prickly Stick Insect Neohirasea catbaensis emits a conspicuous secretion when disturbed, often described as smoky, which constitutes a unique characteristic not known from any other stick and leaf insect. Here we investigate the anatomy and the chemical components of the repellent glands in this species.

pmc-13547665.title: Host-response biomarkers for precision tuberculosis: from immune transcriptomic signatures to clinical risk stratification
pmc-13547665.creator: Nan Yan, Zhen Wang, Shilei Dong, Si Wang, Qinlong Sun, Jiusong Luan
pmc-13547665.description: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major infectious cause of morbidity and mortality, while current diagnostic and treatment-monitoring pathways remain largely pathogen-centered. Microbiological tests are indispensable for confirming TB and detecting drug resistance, but they do not directly measure host inflammatory activity, disease-stage heterogeneity, risk of progression, biological response to therapy, or recurrence after treatment completion.

pmc-13578186.title: Oncolytic virus with an immune stimulatory payload for osteosarcoma therapy
pmc-13578186.creator: Sumbul Khan, Theresa A Higgins, Isabella Shimko-Lofano, Maninder Sandey, Emma Logsdon, Gracie Bunch, Yasin Fatemi, Leah M K Hoffman, Bruce F Smith, Payal Agarwal

pmc-13647549.title: Neuropathy-predominant and hyperkinetic-dystonic presentations in two siblings with a homozygous VPS13A variant: long-term follow-up and family-based clinical analysis
pmc-13647549.creator: Yong Luo, Jian Chen, Tao Ling, Xiaowei Ni, Yandong Xue, Yong Luo
pmc-13647549.description: BackgroundVPS13A disease, historically known as chorea-acanthocytosis, is a rare autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by variable combinations of chorea, dystonia, orolingual involvement, cognitive or psychiatric changes, acanthocytosis, and peripheral neuromuscular abnormalities. Although phenotypic heterogeneity is well recognized, neuropathy-predominant onset may delay diagnostic recognition, particularly before typical hyperkinetic or orolingual features become apparent.
